correctness.rationale: Full-dimensionality is tested as rank four of the four unmarked Boolean vectors after a cube isometry sends the marked vertex to zero. A closest point of a tetrahedron lies on some face and is the exact orthogonal projection of zero onto its affine span; inspecting all 15 nonempty faces with rational nonnegative barycentric feasibility finds the true convex-hull squared distance. The self-contained replay checks all 1,365 fixed-origin choices and 940 valid simplices, their exact 1/4 and 1/3 shells, and exhaustively constructs permutation orbits of sizes 12,12,4, multiplied by 16 marked vertices. Exact arithmetic excludes rounding error; finite exhaustiveness covers the entire finite domain.

value.rationale: The flatness parameter of lattice simplices is a natural polyhedral conditioning invariant. Beyond the already-known optimum 1/2, its next reachable point-to-opposite-face distance for genuine four-dimensional Boolean simplices is unknown from the nearest published papers. A strict first squared-distance gap 1/12 establishes finite stability, and three inequivalent orbit types fully identify all first near-extremizers. The dimension-four finite result is mathematically motivated by the first higher-dimensional Boolean case; no asymptotic extrapolation is asserted.
